title: Tell a two-minute biology story
objective: Tell a short story from six key words. Listen for what changed.

slides.title: Hear a short model
body: First, I found a white butterfly near a flower.
Next, it landed. I saw yellow dust on its legs.
Then it flew to a second flower.
I wondered if it carried pollen there.
What did the speaker see? What was their question?

slides.title: Choose a story
body: Use an observation of your own or retell the butterfly story.
Make four notes: where, first event, next event, why it mattered.
For the model: garden · butterfly · landed · dust · flew · pollen
Choose up to six key words. Leave your full sentences behind.

slides.title: Build your talk
body: Start: Tell your partner where you were and what you saw.
Middle: Use first, next or then to put two events in order.
End: Say what interested you or what you still wonder about.
Use a detail such as colour, size, place or movement.

slides.title: Speak and listen
body: A: Use your key words to speak for up to two minutes.
B: Listen for the two events. Retell them in the same order.
A: Add one missing detail, or correct the order.
Swap roles.

slides.title: Try your ending again
body: Ask your partner: What was the most interesting part?
Use that answer to improve your ending.
Say your final two sentences again without reading.
